question: None shared. P-152 reports cross-sectional diagnosis only (AD vs HC, MCI vs HC, AD vs MCI) from DTI superficial-white-matter features and has no progression task. P-156 predicts which baseline MCI patients progress to dementia by their latest diagnosis. Diagnosis of established AD is not prediction of future dementia among MCI patients.
metric: As recorded, accuracy (95.8%) against AUC (0.81). P-152 also prints AUCs (0.99 AD vs HC, 0.88 MCI vs HC, 0.93 AD vs MCI), so the type could be matched, but not on a shared question.

figures.P-152: AD vs HC accuracy 95.8%, AUC 0.99 (linear SVM, ADNI2 DTI, 24 AD vs 24 HC, internal 5-fold CV). No intervals printed. Hanley-McNeil for AUC 0.99 with 24/24: SE 0.0148 -> 0.961-1.000. Wilson for 95.8% on n=48: 0.860-0.988.
figures.P-156: Held-out test AUC 0.81, F-measure 0.68 (Ensemble Integration, TADPOLE baseline MCI, n=841; test set = 841-672 = 169). Test class split not printed; with the cohort's 34% progressors (about 58/111), Hanley-McNeil SE 0.0377 -> 0.736-0.884.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists: P-152 has no progression result, and P-156 has no cross-sectional AD-vs-HC result.
performance_validity: The cited P-152 value meets the Section 3.5 exclusion when checked against the source: AD vs HC AUC 0.99 (Table 3), n=48, internal 5-fold CV, no external cohort. P-156 (0.81) is not affected.
reason: The record reads P-152's 95.8% as a progression (T2) result, but it is AD vs HC accuracy, and P-152 reports no progression task, so there is no shared clinical question with P-156's future-dementia AUC. The cited P-152 result also meets the near-ceiling exclusion (AUC 0.99, n=48, internal CV only). The intervals are far apart, but that is moot on non-comparable quantities.
